title: Design a Real-Time Voice Agent
summary: A phone agent that listens, thinks and speaks fast enough to feel like a conversation. The design is a latency budget: streaming speech recognition, a fast first token, early speech synthesis, and clean handling of interruptions.
objectives: Turn call volume and call length into concurrent sessions, tokens per day and cost per minute
Build a mouth-to-ear latency budget under about 800 ms and say where each millisecond goes
Choose an endpointing strategy and quantify the trade-off between cut-offs and slow replies
Design barge-in so the agent stops quickly and its memory matches what the caller actually heard
Plan evaluation, safety and failure handling for a live audio system
prerequisites: Work through [A Framework for LLM System Design](/learn/llm-system-design/design-framework) first. You should know TTFT and TPOT from [Measuring Inference](/learn/inference-and-serving/measuring-inference) and prompt caching from [Caching Repeated Work](/learn/inference-and-serving/caching).
